name: The majority voted in favour of a [motion](https://www.openaustralia.org.au/senate/?id=2024-05-16.194.1) to read the bills for a second time (parliamentary jargon for agreeing with the main idea of the bills). This means our senators can now consider the bill in more detail. ### What do the bills do? The [bills digest](https://www.aph.gov.au/Parliamentary_Business/Bills_Legislation/bd/bd2324a/24bd054) set out the following key points: * *The purpose of the [Administrative Review Tribunal Bill 2023](https://www.aph.gov.au/Parliamentary_Business/Bills_Legislation/Bills_Search_Results/Result?bId=r7117) is to establish the [Administrative Review Tribunal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Administrative_Review_Tribunal) (the Tribunal), which will replace the Administrative Appeals Tribunal. The Bill details the Tribunal’s membership, structure, review procedures and other matters. It also re‑establishes the Administrative Review Council.* * *The [Administrative Review Tribunal (Consequential and Transitional Provisions No. 1) Bill 2023](https://www.aph.gov.au/Parliamentary_Business/Bills_Legislation/Bills_Search_Results/Result?bId=r7127) repeals the Administrative Appeals Tribunal Act 1975 and makes consequential amendments to a number of Commonwealth Acts.* * *These Bills were introduced into Parliament on 7 December 2023 and were referred to the [House of Representatives Standing Committee on Social Policy and Legal Affairs](https://www.aph.gov.au/Parliamentary_Business/Committees/House/Social_Policy_and_Legal_Affairs/~/link.aspx?_id=AA0D2BD8399A43CEB91DEBEFD405391F&_z=z) for inquiry and report. The Committee recommended that the House pass the Bills.
